title: Process Engineer
description:
What will you do? Make an impact!


As our new Process Engineer, you'll play a key role in driving continuous improvement and supporting capital investment projects across the site.


Your responsibilities will include:

  • Identifying, developing and delivering continuous improvement initiatives to enhance plant performance, safety and reliability.
  • Supporting capital projects through the full lifecycle, from concept and design through to installation, commissioning, training and ongoing operational support.
  • Working with suppliers and contractors to source equipment, assess capabilities and ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently and cost-effectively.
  • Producing and maintaining technical documentation, specifications and engineering drawings.
  • Collaborating with Operations, Maintenance and SHEQ teams to troubleshoot process issues and implement sustainable solutions.
  • Supporting the planning and execution of plant shutdown activities.
  • Using data, analysis and engineering expertise to optimise processes and improve operational performance.

Do you have what it takes?


We're looking for someone who combines strong technical knowledge with excellent problem-solving and project management skills.


You will ideally have:

  • A degree in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering or a related discipline.
  • Around five years' experience within the chemical, manufacturing or process industries, either in an operational or consultancy environment.
  • Experience managing engineering projects, including contractor selection, scope development, supplier management and project delivery.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to investigate complex challenges and develop practical solutions.
  • A proactive approach to identifying improvement opportunities and driving change.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • A professional, self-motivated and accountable approach to work.


It would be advantageous if you also have:

  • Experience using CAD software.
  • Knowledge of HAZOP, LOPA and area classification studies.
  • Experience working alongside mechanical, civil and control engineering disciplines.
  • Familiarity with project management software such as Microsoft Project.
  • Knowledge of industrial safety and environmental legislation, including DSEAR, COMAH, LOLER, PSSR and the Health & Safety at Work Act.

What's in it for you?

* Competitive salary - £50,000 + Bonus
* 5% annual bonus
* Contributory Pension
* Flexible benefits (access to our benefits platform for discounts and cash back on shopping purchases, gyms and leisure activities, cycle to work scheme and dedicated wellbeing centre)
